purpose: End-to-end differential test of the production GaussianSmallDiskApprox2D path against an independently integrated bivariate-normal probability over a circular hard-body region.

reference.method: bivariate Gaussian probability mass over a circular region
reference.integrator: tensor-product Gauss-Legendre quadrature in polar coordinates
reference.implementation: separate NumPy calculation; does not call Mycelix production code
reference.convergence_note: The stored outputs were stable across all four radial orders to a maximum absolute difference below 4e-19 for these cases.

comparison.tolerance_meaning: 0.2% maximum relative difference between the local-density/small-disk approximation and the independent circular-region integral for these frozen cases only.
comparison.qualification_boundary: Synthetic geometry and covariance exercise the checked state-to-encounter-plane path. This is not NASA MATLAB execution, covariance-realism validation, operational Pc qualification, or maneuver authority.
